## Summary
`context next` accepts inherited context projection/depth flags but neither applies nor validates them. Invalid controls return success and a normal recommendation.

Reproduced with the official installed `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.9.30 on Linux, using disposable synthetic non-Git trackers. No implementation changes are included in this issue.

## Reproduction
```bash
LAB=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$LAB/home" "$LAB/work"
export HOME="$LAB/home" PM_PATH="$LAB/work/.agents/pm"
export PM_GLOBAL_PATH="$LAB/global" PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
cd "$LAB/work"
pm init "$PM_PATH" --defaults --author audit --agent-guidance skip --json >/dev/null
pm create task "Audit sample" --id t1 --description "Execution detail" --json >/dev/null
```
```bash
pm context next --json
pm context next --fields id,title,description --json
pm context next --fields notafield --json
pm context next --depth nonsense --json
```

## Actual
All commands exit 0. The same recommendation shape is returned: 17 fields, including fields not requested by the explicit projection, while the stored description remains absent. An unknown projection and a nonsensical depth receive no typed error or ignored-option warning.

## Expected and impact
A supported option must be applied and validated. If a parent option has no meaning on a child command, reject it with a typed actionable error before executing the command. Silent acceptance teaches agents an incorrect contract and can withhold explicitly requested execution detail.

## Implementation plan
1. Inventory parent/global option inheritance versus child handlers and declared flag contracts.
2. Define supported projection/depth semantics for next; reuse the shared projection validator and renderer where appropriate.
3. Explicitly reject unsupported inherited controls rather than silently swallowing them.
4. Generate help/contract applicability from the same registry used by dispatch validation.
5. Add parent-flags × subcommands tests, with representative valid and invalid values, and CLI/MCP parity for supported features.

## Regression acceptance
- [ ] An id/title/description projection returns the requested stored description and documented mandatory metadata, or is explicitly rejected as unsupported
- [ ] Unknown fields and invalid depth return nonzero typed errors
- [ ] Parent flag placement and aliases do not change validation
- [ ] Recommended and companion rows follow one documented projection rule
- [ ] Tests cover other inherited controls to catch accepted-but-unused flags
- [ ] No regression to next ranking, blocker visibility or token-budget enforcement

## Ownership and duplicate check
Child of #1363; conformance coverage for #1361/#1362. Closed #440/#156 concerned context projection availability; this is the nested next dispatch path. Closed #1264 concerned token-budget enforcement and is distinct. Searched open and closed context-next, fields and depth issues.
GH-1368: Agent UX: context next silently ignores inherited --fields and --depth options, including invalid values

Reported agent-facing contract defect imported from https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1368. Preserve existing shipped foundations. Detailed source observations are dated 2026-09-30 and must be revalidated before implementation.

An id/title/description projection returns the requested stored description and documented mandatory metadata, or is explicitly rejected as unsupported; Unknown fields and invalid depth return nonzero typed errors; Parent flag placement and aliases do not change validation; Recommended and companion rows follow one documented projection rule; Tests cover other inherited controls to catch accepted-but-unused flags; No regression to next ranking, blocker visibility or token-budget enforcement
The public command follows the documented equivalent-option, receipt or recovery contract without changing valid unrelated behavior.
Source report reproduced published 2026.9.30 behavior; current checkout requires fresh reproduction before claiming the defect.
